hypothesis: Keeping the baseline 128-thread shared-memory reduction tree while storing every partial in int64 should preserve exact cancellation behavior. A bounded finalizer handles up to 1024 partials; larger arrays get parallel reduction stages. This adaptive topology may reduce full-call cost by avoiding recursive work and the final copy for ordinary sizes, while not assigning the full large input to one CTA. It remains a performance hypothesis until measured.
notes: The only measured comparator available is baseline-e1: correct, with three full-call samples averaging 46.4832 microseconds. The T1 catalog has no prior records or source-diversity evidence, so there are no earlier T1 candidates to compare. This candidate has not been measured, and no failed variant data is available; controller evaluation is needed for repeated full-call results.
transformations: Generalized the baseline reduction kernel to read int values into int64 accumulators while retaining its 128-thread shared-memory tree.
Added a direct exact one-CTA path for up to 128 values; for larger inputs, first emits 128-value int64 partials into scratch.
Finalizes at most 1024 partials in one CTA writing directly to out; recursively adds parallel 128-way partial stages above that bound using two packed scratch buffers.
Uses no scratch reads before writes and launches work on the default stream; narrows to int only after the true total is formed.
